items.en: With ⟦0⟧, the Raj has a sprawling focus tree that can be very powerful, but is also full of "trap" options that appear beneficial on paper but end up being detrimental in practice. Examples of these "trap" options include Swadeshi Movement (whose long completion time, increased resistance target, and lack of meaningful unlocks end up making the one ⟦1⟧ and pitiful autonomy increase it provides not worth it), Princely States Policy (whose ⟦2⟧ do not actually provide any meaningful benefits after accounting for the misleading way the game handles ⟦3⟧), and Defense Of India Act (which does not provide any real benefits over sticking to ⟦4⟧ at peace-time and ⟦5⟧ at wartime even if it can be taken early thanks to the Axis powers generating a lot of early World Tension). It can also be very easy to inadvertently sabotage Raj's build by taking certain focuses too early, e.g., taking Agricultural Cooperatives before it gives at least 2 ⟦6⟧ or taking military factory focuses too early and therefore wasting their size increase effects for key military industrial organizations on smaller sizes that would require fewer funds to increase normally, thus unnecessarily delaying the incredibly powerful The Ordnance Factories Board. It is therefore important to prioritize: focus on economy- and research-related focuses early, pivot to military factory-related focuses afterwards, and then focus on picking up the numerous stats bonuses that Raj has in their new focus tree, including from Lions of the Great War, Model After Soviet Union, Specialized Dietary Requirement, Inclusive Nationalism, and South East Asia Command (the bonuses of which are contained in an event that fires immediately after its completion). Special attention should also be paid to For the People, By the People, as its research bonuses can be used to get earlier access to critical infantry weapon technologies, usually either ⟦7⟧ or ⟦8⟧ depending on who else is rushing those technologies on the Allies. Acquiring ⟦9⟧ status and, eventually, freedom is still helpful and can be done with the same convoy lend-lease tricks as without the DLC, but is not as vital to get done as early as possible as it is without the DLC. Once all stat bonuses have been acquired, it is likely a good idea to pick up as many focuses that will prevent the spread of famine. The Bengal Famine is especially devastating with ⟦10⟧, and reaching 100% famine spread prevention as early as possible is vital to making sure it only lasts 6-10 months instead of the years that it can otherwise last. Remember to have ⟦11⟧ researched before the famine starts to be able to immediately use the decision unlocked by Quinine.

Without ⟦0⟧, the Raj has a smaller focus tree, with focuses that are both lengthy and relatively weak compared to other nations'. It is important to make the most of the tree, focusing on unlocking their third research slot and gaining enough war support to pass ⟦1⟧ early. Rushing to complete Quit India Movement and Two-Nation Theory may seem wasteful, but they stop and slowly reverse the passive autonomy decline Raj experiences from the start of the game, which can allow them to take more investment focuses later without jeopardizing their position. The choice of what to use Vickers-Berthier Gun on can also be important, with ⟦2⟧ usually being such a good candidate that Raj should often rush to try to get that technology as early as possible with the help of that focus. Once WW2 starts, it is imperative to lend-lease the ⟦3⟧ convoys to achieve ⟦4⟧ status early enough to complete Clamp Down On Corruption before the Bengal Famine starts (300 days after WW2 starts), then to eventually become independent and be able to reduce the penalties of Agrarian Society after taking Administrative Oversight. If Raj runs out of convoys to lend-lease, have other Commonwealth nations like ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧, and ⟦7⟧ send Raj theirs; the ⟦8⟧ can also lend-lease them its convoys so that they can forward them to Raj who can send them back to the ⟦9⟧. Achieving ⟦10⟧ status early is also important to be able to complete Indian Gentlemen Officers, which, together with ⟦11⟧, will allow Raj to fix their shortage of generals with newly recruited ones who are often better than the ones with which it starts.

Regardless of DLCs, Raj has to deal with limited research slots for most of the game, as well as potential ⟦0⟧ issues. The upside is that the land fronts they are expected to have with ⟦1⟧ tend to be quite rugged, filled with ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, and ⟦4⟧ provinces (though perhaps unexpectedly, no ⟦5⟧ provinces outside of a handful in Burma). For these reasons, it is usually a good idea to take the Mass Mobilization side of the ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧, to lean heavily into land units with terrain bonuses in these provinces like ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧, and ⟦10⟧, and to try to get early access to both ⟦11⟧ and ⟦12⟧ to make the ⟦13⟧ and ⟦14⟧ units fielded in these provinces as powerful as they can be. Technology choices should be triaged because of the low research slot count, as Raj simply cannot afford to pick up useful but otherwise luxury options like ⟦15⟧ or ⟦16⟧ without denying themselves timely access to other, more critical technologies. If ⟦17⟧ issues can be overcome, e.g., through reducing the impact of Agrarian Society earlier and/or more or saving up a lot of ⟦18⟧ to switch to ⟦19⟧, the Infiltration side of ⟦20⟧ or the Shock and Awe side of ⟦21⟧ can also work for ⟦22⟧ choices, though care should be taken to deploy units with highly upgraded ⟦23⟧ to avoid ⟦24⟧. It is also important to make sure Raj's few ports are fully garrisonned against any naval invasions that ⟦25⟧ might attempt once they stop making progress over land.

Capturing factories from the Axis means that the British investment focuses are not worth it for the player in single-player, since these focuses greatly slow down independence and the rewards from these focuses are a pittance compared to what can be captured (also the railroad construction bonus is lost on independence). Two-Nation Theory and Quit India Movement are also not worth it (unless one is aiming for the “Our Words Are Backed With Nuclear Weapons” achievement). Remember that autonomy is being lost passively for India every day, meaning each extra focus has an additional autonomy cost. Cripps' Mission must be taken to get dominion status, despite its bad effects. Pakistan and Burma can be released as puppets when the player gets a notification of unrest in the northwest and northeast in order to avoid civil war.

Your main aim as the Raj in historical multiplayer is to defend against ⟦0⟧ for as long as possible. How this is best done depends on the game's rules, active DLCs, and how ⟦1⟧ acts in their war against ⟦2⟧. A ⟦3⟧ that blazes through ⟦4⟧ to conquer it quickly will have access to more ⟦5⟧ and ⟦6⟧ for longer but will tend to have less experienced generals due to the lack of ⟦7⟧ opportunities, while a ⟦8⟧ that takes their time will tend to have far more powerful generals and field marshals from ⟦9⟧, and therefore far better stats on their units, at the cost of delaying their access to the rather substantial Chinese industrial base. Time is also usually on the Allies' side, so the longer it takes for ⟦10⟧ to declare war, the easier it should be to deal with them once they have.

The most efficient way to gain the autonomy needed for dominion and independence is war contribution and lend-leasing to the ⟦0⟧. Both war contribution and lend-lease material can be gained very early in the war through a naval invasion of Italy originating from southern ⟦1⟧ (before ⟦2⟧ is invaded by Germany) and then capitulation of ⟦3⟧. In single-player, ⟦4⟧ really is the “soft underbelly of Europe”. The captured war materials can then be shipped to the ⟦5⟧ to increase autonomy. The player must finish Clamp Down On Corruption within 300 days of the start of WWII in order assure the Bengal Famine is avoided. A rapid capitulation of ⟦6⟧ has the additional advantage of tipping the balance of power between Allies and Axis enough that ⟦7⟧ can hold off the German invasion.

The British Raj in 1936 is beset with communal divisions between the Hindus and the Muslims, and the Burmese in the extreme east outright rejects any affinity with the Raj, insisting that they are a separate nation that was unreasonably incorporated into the Raj by the British only because of geographical proximity. In the game, this is represented by the states of Peshawar, Punjab, Quetta, Baluchistan and Sind in the west, and Mandalay and Burma in the east being classified as occupied states, which significantly reduces the amount of manpower, resources, and industrial capacity the player can utilize from these states.

During World War II, British India fielded the largest volunteer army in the war, and used it to contain the Japanese advance into Burma, as well as stopping Japanese advances into the Indian subcontinent. The Battle of Imphal was a critical victory that stopped the ⟦0⟧ army's advances from occupied Burma. The war, however, was not without consequences to the people of the Raj, as wartime needs for the military often superseded any civilian concerns. A massive famine in the Bengal region was blamed upon the limited food aid sent by the British in favor of sending those supplies to the European and African theaters.

The British Raj was the result of piecemeal annexation of Indian princely states by the British East India Company. After a series of failed mutinies in 1857, the British Government took control of India from the BEIC and the Raj was born with Queen Victoria being given the title of Empress of India. Modern day India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Myanmar form part of the British Raj in 1936. Although some territories like Rajputana were independently governed under British suzerainty, they have been abstracted under the overall control of the Raj for game play purposes.

The British Raj suffered politically during the war as different groups vied to command leadership of the then flourishing Indian independence movement. The Muslim League and the Indian National Congress disagreed on their opinions on supporting the British war effort, with the League backing the British and Congress calling for supporting the British in exchange for concessions. Eventually, the British government agreed to consider Indian independence after the war ended. The last Viceroy of India, Louis Mountbatten, left in 1947, just two years after the war.

The Five Year Plan Sub-branch This section of the Reds in the Shadows Sub-branch builds up Indian industry based on a The Five Year Plan. Depending on the player's choice in the previous section, Agrarian Socialism will lead to an Independent India with Peasant armies and production bonuses and compliance. Choosing Urban Industrialism will side with the Soviets and focus on a liberation army, as well as research cooperation with the Soviets and Military factory construction. The final focus Continue the Five Year Plan will multiply all modifiers by 30%.

With so few ⟦0⟧ and many resources, trade is important for the Raj in the early game for gaining more civilian industrial points, allowing India to build up its industry to rival that of some of the less industrialized great powers. However, as long as the Raj remains a ⟦1⟧ of the ⟦2⟧, it cannot remove risk of famine, and until it becomes independent, it cannot take advantage of its large manpower and cannot access 2 of its 5 research slots. Therefore, quickly gaining ⟦3⟧ status and independence should be top priorities of the player.

The British Raj will be behind technologically until independence so pick one or two aspects of your military (such as the air force) to do very well and get ahead-of-time to compensate for weaknesses elsewhere. India remains part of Commonwealth Tech Sharing with full bonuses even after independence so its research could very well eventually become ⟦0⟧ than any other country's (besides the ⟦1⟧) once all 5 research slots are unlocked. Further boosts can be picked up by stealing blueprints while getting the "Spies Trade" achievement.

Reds in the Shadows Sub-branch This Communist sub-branch, after a civil war, turns India into a Communist state. It may then either choose to focus on Agrarian Socialism which would develop rural states, or choose Urban Industrialism allowing industrial expansion and dams in the urban states. cooperation with the Soviets or forming an independent path, as well as providing various army and industry bonuses and granting war goals against imperialist powers.

An AI ⟦0⟧ pursuing a Southern Expansion strategy will become a threat to India around 1942 or so (assuming the war in Europe has not already been won). However, India is at the limit of ⟦1⟧’s naval reach and is defended by mountain and jungle terrain so not many forces are needed to stop ⟦2⟧ (a few ships in the Bay of Bengal can prevent naval invasion). Just make sure your defensive lines are supplied and entrenched.

Forward Bloc Sub-branch This sub-branch allows a violent overthrow of the British, providing bonuses against them such as infilitrating Aden which eventually ends in a white peace agreement, and allows India to pursue the Azad Hind approach, gaining help from the Japanese and joining their faction. It also opens the Netaji and Hindutva sub-branches, allowing the player a choice between them.

Netaji Sub-branch This sub-branch keeps Bose as leader of India, providing bonuses in mountains, as well as providing a choice of Authoriatianism or Guided Democracy and a cooperation with the Soviets or the Axis, which allows India to become either Communist or Fascist, reflecting Bose's historical pragmatism as well as giving wargoals against China, Nepal and Bhutan.

This branch builds dockyards and naval bases, grants bonuses to researching better naval models, unlocks and upgrades MIOs, gives naval experience, provides bonuses to air and marines and unlocks unique ship models. It also offers a choice between relying on the ⟦0⟧, buying ships from them and gaining naval commanders or allowing India to venture on its own.

This branch upgrades artillery, armor, granting army buffs and unlocking new divisions as well as the ability to make the ⟦0⟧ army more adept in mountainous terrain, both for tanks, artillery and infantry. It also grants buffs to supply consumption, and allows Quinine which both helps with the ⟦1⟧ and also grants unique bonuses.

I Am Death Sub-branch This hidden sub-branch, only available if Gandhi survives his assassination attempt, puts Gandhi in charge of India and allowing the player to to play as an aggressive Democracy that provides bonuses to Nuclear research and grants Nuclear-powered bonuses to the army.

Tryst with Destiny Sub-branch This sub-branch allows the British Raj to choose between joining the Allies or remaining neutral, then continuing on to consolidate the new state, annex Goa and French India, as well as providing considerable economic and research bonuses.

This branch gives ⟦0⟧ the choice of either relying on ⟦1⟧ generals, as well as receiving military equipment, spy bonuses and other bonuses from the ⟦2⟧, or Indianizing the army, and modelling after one of the other big majors, gaining unique themed bonuses.

The ⟦0⟧ (modern-day India) is a ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ in South Asia with a core population of ⟦3⟧ and an additional ⟦4⟧ non-core. It borders ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧, ⟦11⟧, and ⟦12⟧, colonial provinces of ⟦13⟧ and ⟦14⟧ as well as ⟦15⟧ and ⟦16⟧ via Province of Aden.

The military path of the loyalty branch allows the British Raj to go to war with ⟦0⟧ enemies and ⟦1⟧. It will build defenses in Aden, and other ⟦2⟧ colonial states, gain terrain specialties, and the possible annexation of those colonial states.

The ⟦0⟧ loyalty brings Independence through loyalty. All three sections must be completed to become ⟦1⟧. The Leftmost path focuses on politics, from choosing leadership; Gandhi, Nehru or Churchill; to managing local princes and the Muslims.

This ⟦0⟧ sub-branch begins by destabilizing the nation, and declaring war against the British Raj from the west. It may then choose its new leader as the Sultanate of Al-Hind and then gain military, research and industrial bonuses.

In both the 1936 and 1939 scenarios, the non-aligned Indian National Congress is the ruling political party in the British Raj with Lord Linlithgow acting as the Governor-General and Viceroy of India with overwhelming popularity.

Vertical Integration Sub-branch This part of the sub-branch focuses on modifying the taxes and tax brackets to benefit the East India Company. It culminates in War Goals on Communist powers as well as the United Kingdom.

This unique sub-branch switches the player to the East India Company, transforming into a corporation that can purchase and core land from other countries, granting plenty of bonuses to army, economy and resources,

This independence branch allows the British Raj to gradually go independent from the British, as well as granting many bonuses to research and the economy. It also opens all the subsequent political branches.

It is possible to leave the Commonwealth. India can choose to join the Comintern or Axis via the Swaraj branch of its national focus tree. This will lead to a civil war which will be backed by its new allies.

The ⟦0⟧ has a number of unique names for various technologies and equipment, listed here. Particularly Commonwealth armaments, including their own Armored Equipment. Note that generic names are not listed.

Revolt of the Princes Sub-branch This path focuses on bringing the Princely States as puppets against the British Raj, unite the Indian Subcontinent and ultimately declare war against the United Kingdom.
This branch builds railways throughout ⟦0⟧, where the more focuses you complete the faster you can build things like supply hubs, railways and infrastructure. It also provides some extra resources.
The ⟦0⟧ got a unique national focus tree as part of the ⟦1⟧ expansion. Ever since the DLC's integration, it is now available in the base game. With ⟦2⟧, It gained a completely revamped focus tree.
Rani Of Jhansi Regiment Sub-branch The focus shared with the Fascist/Non-aligned path and the Communist path recruits an all women regiment, allowing more Recruitable population and a General.
This branch builds military factories in ⟦0⟧, with each Ordinance factory unlocking extra traits for the MIO as well. Finishing the focus branch awards the player with an upgraded MIO policy.
This branch grants bonuses to researching better aircraft models, unlocks and upgrades MIOs, gives air experience, provides bonuses to air and paratroopers and unlocks unique aircraft models.
Form A Security Force Sub-branch The military path for the East India Company builds up the army and navy as well as give industrial bonuses and War Goals on India's neighboring countries.
Timurid Bureaucracy Sub-branch This path sets the country to expand around Asia against Iran, Iraq, Mongolia, Afghanistan, Sinkiang and the Soviet Union and restore the Timurid Empire.
The ⟦0⟧ starts with a small and under-equipped army, as well as a small air force. It does not possess a navy. The available manpower is heavily restricted by the ⟦1⟧ national spirit.

This branch opens the Mughal and East India Company branches, providing quick relief to the ⟦0⟧ but destabilizing the country in the process.
With the ⟦0⟧ expansion enabled, the British Raj also begins with the ⟦1⟧ national spirit, and the effects of ⟦2⟧ are significantly modified:
Take as much as possible in peace negotiations to propel India to major power status and perhaps even leadership of the Allied faction.
This branch deals with granting manpower and working towards the reduction and eventual removal of the ⟦0⟧ national spirit.
Coal, Fire and Steel Sub-branch The focuses shared between the expansionist and the Bose paths give industrial bonuses.
This alternative, Anti-Gandhi independence sub-branch pushes India into an expansionist ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧ or ⟦2⟧ path.
